findings.title: ka0s-bounded timeout kills only the top process, then reports the run as stopped
findings.evidence: timeout --foreground signals only the direct child; forked children survive and keep the slot-pool lock fd (opened :78). Reproduced: KA0S_KIT_TIMEOUT_S=2 KA0S_KIT_CGROUP=off ka0s-bounded bash -c 'sleep 47; echo done' -> rc=124 'was stopped', pgrep still lists sleep 47; same with systemd scope (sleep 53 survivor). Softened in collection: LibKa0s kit gives each Lua process its own timeout. No timeout test case.
findings.remediation: C-01: use --foreground only when stdin is a TTY ([ -t 0 ]) so timeout signals the whole process group otherwise; update header comment and DEPENDENCIES.md:47; add BinWrapper.test_timeout_kills_children (20->21 cases, CLAUDE.md:91).

findings.title: ka0s-bounded computes the slot count once, before the wait loop
findings.evidence: slots=$(( avail_mb*6/10/slot_mb )) computed once; poll loop only probes slot.1..slot.$slots. A caller started under memory pressure with slots=1 waits for slot.1 even after memory frees; runs serialize more than needed in parallel sweeps.
findings.remediation: C-08: recompute slots (re-read MemAvailable) inside the wait loop; explicit KA0S_KIT_SLOTS still wins; print 'waiting' once.
